text: olivia: Weird failure in linkcheck: fragments with slashes or brackets in headings are getting mangled after MDX swap. Example: /guides/auth#oauth/flow and /api#rate-limit[per-user] both 404. ben: Can you paste snippets? olivia: From guides/auth.md: ```markdown ### OAuth/Flow Steps for exchange... ``` And from api/limits.md: ```markdown ### Rate limit [per-user] Limit examples... ``` tai: I can repro locally. The slugifier drops or replaces special chars inconsistently. OAuth/Flow -> oauthflow-1 sometimes; Rate limit [per-user] -> rate-limit-per-user-1. Old links were plain `#oauth/flow` and `#rate-limit[per-user]`. harper: CI output: ``` [linkcheck] ERROR: Fragment not found: https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/auth#oauth/flow [linkcheck] ERROR: Fragment not found: https://docs.redwood.ai/api#rate-limit[per-user] ``` ben: Short term: add explicit anchors with normalized ids. Eg: ```html ### OAuth/Flow ### Rate limit [per-user] ``` That preserves old external linking if we also add redirects or update links. olivia: I'll push a tiny PR adding anchors to the two pages and add a migration note in docs/migration/SPECIAL-CHAR-ANCHORS.md advising maintainers to avoid special chars in headings or add anchors. tai: Long-term we should normalize slug generation to percent-encode or replace brackets/slashes consistently and add a migration script to rewrite incoming internal links. I'll file DOCS-801. Also add unit tests for headings with /, [, ], and parentheses. docs-bot: Deploy preview for fix branch: https://deploy-preview-1500--staging.docs.redwood.ai (build 1500) :white_check_mark: linkcheck shows those two pages fixed. harper: Nice. After merge let's run a full-site linkcheck and grep for headings with these chars: `git grep -n "### .*[/\[\]]" docs/` and batch fixes. olivia: PR opened: redwood/docs#3577 1 1 (assigns: olivia; reviewers: ben, tai). Thanks all.
